506200000.name: Ginubat Festival
506200000.description: A festival based on the roots of the town of which its name was derived. It features cultural street parade, exhibit, sail boat race, beauty pageant, fiesta celebration, etc.

506200000.name: Magalleones Festival
506200000.description: The festival depicts the reputation of the municipality as one of the shipbuilding capitals of the Bicol peninsula during the Spanish colonial period. The celebration honors its Patroness, Our Lady of Mt Cam1el and is highlighted by colorful street dance presentations.

506200000.name: Hin-ay Festival
506200000.description: This features a cultural show, trade fair, and a street dance depicting the archangels’ victory over the “Black” Angels.

506200000.name: Parau Festival
506200000.description: A 12–day celebration done simultaneously with the Feast of Our Lady of the Pillar. It showcases the town’s cultural heritage and the growing aspirations of its people. During this event. families, relatives and friends get together, renew kinship and enjoy the festivities.

506200000.name: Unod Festival
506200000.description: “Unod” Festival expresses thanksgiving of the people of Castilla, a celebration of the bountiful harvest of root crops of the town and the value of being industrious people.· The festival’s highlight is the street dancing competition.

600400000.name: Ati-Atihan Festival
600400000.description: Street festival with tribal face paint honoring the Santo Niño.

600400000.name: Ati – Atihan Festival
600400000.description: This is an ancient tradition that celebrates the people of Aklan with indigenous origins, eventually honoring the Infant Jesus, Señor Santo Niño. Today, the Ati-Atihan is observed in modern times as a festival dedicated to the Child Jesus. The term “Ati-Atihan” means “merry-making like the Ati,” referring to becoming like the aboriginal natives who are considered the first inhabitants of Aklan and the entire Western Visayas region. Participants smear themselves with soot to darken their skin and dress in tribal finery, complete with the festival’s iconic tasseled headdresses. The procession begins with the vibrant beat of drums and prominent whistles, later punctuated by energetic shouts of “Hala Bira!” followed by “Viva kay Señor Santo Niño!”

location.text: rd Sunday of January Kalibo, Aklan

600600000.name: Karanowan Fish-Tival
600600000.description: In appreciation of the beautiful God- given nature, the Karonawan Fish-Tival is a celebration of the beauty and bounty of Bato in order to inject and instill the importance of preserving and conserving the these natural resources as major sources of food and as potential tourist attractions.

603000000.name: Dinagyang Festival
603000000.description: Warrior-painted tribes dance in honor of the Santo Niño.

603000000.name: The Dinagyang Festival
603000000.description: Dinagyang is a Hiligaynon word extrapolated from dagyang meaning “merrymaking” It celebrates the feast of the Infant Jesus and the pact between the Datus and the locals.

607900000.name: Ang Pagtaltal
607900000.description: This is a procession of flagellants and devotees in biblical attire that ends in the Balaan Bukid Shrine.

607900000.name: Pangalap Ritual
607900000.description: This is a ritual where believers crawl through the Catilaran cave chanting prayers in the hope of gaining supernatural powers to ward off evil spirits.

701200000.name: Sandugo Festival
701200000.description: Commemorates the blood compact between Sikatuna and Legazpi.

702200000.name: Sinulog Festival
702200000.description: Grand festival honoring the Santo Niño with street dancing and fluvial parade.

702200000.name: Anibina Bulawanun Festival
702200000.description: This is an eight-day multi-themed annual festival that culminates on the province’s foundation day, March 8. It is a colorful and joyful celebration of the province’s rich agricultural harvests, abundant mineral resources, governance’s feats, trade and tourism fair, and a showcasing of the people’s culture and traditions. The Al-law Ng Kalomonan (Tribal Day) falls on the 7th day of Anibina.

704600000.name: Sinulog de Tanjay Festival
704600000.description: The celebration of the residents of Tanjay, Negros Oriental of this 10-day fiesta features the origin of the old sinulog culture. A parade is held showcasing the clothes locals wear, while the horsefighting presentation re-enacts the battle between the Spaniards and the Muslims.

704600000.name: Aurora Festival
704600000.dateVenueRaw: last Sunday of August to first week of September Tanjay, Negros Oriental
704600000.description: The festival features evening novenas participated in by more than 40 clans, which culminate in a nocturnal fluvial procession at the Tanjay River.

location.text: last Sunday of August to first week of September Tanjay, Negros Oriental

704600000.name: Pasko sa Tanjay Festival
704600000.description: This is a month-long Christmas festivity featuring cultural presentations and contests..

803700000.name: Pintados-Kasadyaan Festival
803700000.description: Body-paint festival honoring pre-colonial warrior traditions.

907200000.name: Seafoods Festival
907200000.description: Kagang is a crab specie common to seven (7) coastal barangays of Dapitan comprising Taguillon, Banbanan, Carang & Baylimango. Kagang Festival started way back February 2014 and is celebrated annually since then. The festival features the traditional way of cooking kagang which will be offered for visitor experience. The event was organized to revive the waning interest and preserve authentic and traditional flavorful dishes where kagang is the main ingredient.

907200000.name: Kinabayo Festival
907200000.dateVenueRaw: July 23-27 Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte
907200000.description: Kinabayo is an annual observance of Dapitan City’s Fiesta in honor of Saint James “the Greater and the Moor Slayer”. Held every July, Sinug and Kinabayo have become a festivity. Sinug’ is purely veneration using San Francisco Leaves raised high, dancing through the rhythm of the gong or beating of drums as the throng of devotees brings the saint’s image to his chapel. On the other hand, Kinabayo is a unique dramatization of the triumph of the Catholic faith over Mohammedanism believed to have happened through the intercession of the saint in view of his apparition during the battles of Clavijo and Covadonga and the appearance of the Lady of the Pilar. Modernity has added more color to the festival with the allegorical dance drama presentation of the two events.

location.text: July 23-27 Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte

907200000.name: Dahunog sa Dipolog
907200000.dateVenueRaw: September 26- October 07 Dipolog City, Region IX
907200000.description: “Dahunog” is one of the most ceLebrated festivals in Dipolog where marching bands converge for a parade and compete by showcasing talents to produce the most thunderous, lively and entertaining musical revelry.’ Dahunog [da.ht.i.nug.}is a Cebuano word which means rumbling sound. During the event the city streets resonate with the sounds played by the bands specially the drums, thus the name of the festival.

location.text: September 26- October 07 Dipolog City, Region IX

907200000.name: Universal Children’s Festival
907200000.description: The festival involves children of locals, dressed in costumes of UN member countries, parading around the city.

907300000.name: Pasalamat Festival
907300000.description: Celebrated annually every 3rd Sunday of January in honor of Sr. Santo Nino and in commemoration of the arrival of the saint’s image in the Philippines and in the City of Pagadian. The Catholic Church spearheads re­ enacbnent on the arrival of the Sto. Nino image through procession. Pasalamat Festival is highlighted with a fluvial parade (regatta), trade exhibits. the Mutya ng Pagadian beauty pageant, carnival shows as well a a civic military parade.

location.text: rd Week of January Pagadian City

907300000.name: Kamgbegu Festival (Fest of the Harvest)
907300000.dateVenueRaw: October15-16,2020 Lapuyan, Zamboanga del Sur (Municipal), Region IX
907300000.description: A festival celebrated by people of Duhaylungsod Lapuyan, Zamboanga del Sur who are well known for their peace-loving nature. Through the years, the Subanen’s main source of living is planting rice which is an important aspect of their culture. For the Subanen, harvest season is a time for merrymaking where they come together as one, family and friends, not only for the harvest but also sharing of bountiful blessing, singing, dancing, chanting and feasting altogether on home-made delicacies and ‘pangase’, a rice wine fermented through a traditional process kept and handed down through ancestral lines. The celebration happens every October in time for the harvest season.

location.text: October15-16,2020 Lapuyan, Zamboanga del Sur (Municipal), Region IX

907300000.name: Kawayanan Festival
907300000.dateVenueRaw: 3rd week Capitol Complex, Pagadian, Zamboanga del Sur
907300000.description: This celebrates the versatility of the Bamboo plant and its importance in the area.

location.text: rd week Capitol Complex, Pagadian, Zamboanga del Sur

908300000.name: Sibug-Sibug Festival and Founding Anniversary of Zamboanga Sibugay Province
908300000.description: A weeklong celebration of Sibugaynon (people of Zamboanga Sibugay) is a commemoration of its founding day as a Province. Sibug – Sibug Festival is celebrated every February with its highlight fixed on February 26. During the event, the streets are decked with colorful buntings and filled with throng of onlookers waiting for the colorful street dancing depicting wedding and healing rituals, way of life of indigenous people groups, and themes to communicate advocacies.

1001300000.name: Spring Festival
1001300000.description: A Festival to celebrate the bounty of springs “tuburan” in the area which serves as their major drive for tourism activity and staple income through different mountain resorts. The event is highlighted with a street dancing competition with their own renditions of the story, giving life to how a municipality’s bountiful springs are created participated by different barangays.

1001800000.name: Panaad
1001800000.description: During the Holy Week, devotees journey to Camiguin island and hike around the 64 km circumferential road as form of sacrifice either in fulfilment of a vow or as penance of sins. Masses, Catholic rites and rituals, Stations of the Cross in the Old Vulcan hill are regular activities during this season.

1001800000.name: San Juan sa Hibok-Hibok Festival
1001800000.description: Held annually every June 24 to honor St. John the Baptist with fluvial procession, parade and water sports.

1003500000.name: MassKara Festival
1003500000.description: Festival of smiling masks and street dancing.

1003500000.name: Nangkaan Festival
1003500000.dateVenueRaw: February 27 - CANCELLED Maigo , Lanao del Norte
1003500000.description: Celebration of Lanao’s abundance in the Municipality of Maigo through street dancing competition with aqua and agro fair. The search for Ms. Maigo and fashion show using langka is the highlight for promotion of the area.

location.text: February 27 - CANCELLED Maigo , Lanao del Norte

1003500000.name: Alimango Festival
1003500000.description: An annual celebration that highlights the abundance of Crabs in the Municipality of Lala. Activities include a crab/ocean themed grand street dancing parade, crab races, biggest crab contest and an agri-trade fair

1003500000.name: Hugyaw Sa Kadagatan
1003500000.description: Thanksgiving for the bountiful harvest in line with the Municipality’s foundation day and fiesta which highlight a fluvial parade participated by different barangays in the area.

1003500000.name: Lechonan sa Baroy
1003500000.description: A celebration of bounty of agricultural products with a grand parade of Lechon” – (roasted pig) in the town plaza ornamented with various farm products to showcase the areas rich harvest.

1003500000.name: Masskara Festival
1003500000.description: This is a grand Bacoleño celebration marked by carnivals, fairs and masked street dancers.

1003500000.name: Kahumayan Festival
1003500000.description: A tribute to the hardworking, industrious, rice farmers who contributed to the development and prosperity of the municipality. “Humay” is a Visaya word for rice that is abundant in the area (white rice/black rice).

1004200000.name: Festival of Lights Tangub City Charter Day
1004200000.description: A spectacular show of dancing lights is showcased through mass performances of elementary and high school students. Float and arch contests are also held during this time which is participated both by the government and the private sector.

1004200000.name: Subayan Keg Subanen Festival
1004200000.description: A street dancing and tableau competition which highlights the lifestyles of the Subanons as depicted in songs and dances, and other forms of simulated social expressions, participated by different private schools, 51 Barangays and government contingents using creative costumes and props. It commemorates the anniversary of Ozamiz becoming a chartered city in July 16, 1948. The date also coincides the “FEAST OF OUR LADY OF MT. CARMEL”, the second patroness of the city. It commemorates the anniversary of Ozamiz City becoming a chartered city in July 16, 1948.

1004200000.name: Christmas Symbols
1004200000.description: A beautiful Christmas Display in Tangub City, the Christmas Symbols Capital of the Philippines is a holiday tradition inspired by love, value for arts and culture exemplified by the illustrious people of the city through this annual event. How would you like to travel the world while enjoying the holiday season’s lights and colors? At this laid-back city in Northern Mindanao “Tangub City”, you get a passport to be filled with country stamps when you visit famous landmarks adorned with Christmas lights and colors.

1004300000.name: Kuyamis Festival
1004300000.dateVenueRaw: January 6-11 Provincial Capitol ground, MIs. Or.
1004300000.description: Kuyamis Festival is the grandest festival in Misamis Oriental, gathering all its towns & cities in Cagayan de Oro City for a week-long non-stop merrymaking. One of the activities that highlight the event is the Kuyamis Festival Street Dancing . It is an annual festivity of thanksgiving and acknowledgment to the customs of the “lumads” who thrived in Misamis with a variety of sweet coconuts as their best food stuff.

location.text: January 6-11 Provincial Capitol ground, MIs. Or.

1004300000.name: Diyandi Festival
1004300000.dateVenueRaw: 3rd Monday of January Balingasag, Misamis Oriental
1004300000.description: A celebration of songs, culture and heritage of the Higaonon Tribes of Balingasag.

location.text: rd Monday of January Balingasag, Misamis Oriental

1004300000.name: Patunob Festival
1004300000.description: A popular religious festival where devotees flock to the shrine of Birhen sa Lourdes to light candles to renew their vows and ask for petitions and blessings. Part of the festival are procession, parade, cultural show, and trade fair. Patunob sa Birhen sa Lourdes is a ritual of healing officiated by women healer devotees of Binuangan. To add, Patunob is a Visayan word for “to be stepped on”. It is a rite where the image of the Blessed Virgin is lightly placed on the person’s shoulders & head.

1004300000.name: Grand Kaliga Festival
1004300000.description: This colorful and joyous festival of abundance and prosperity stems from the city’s Manobo and Higaonon roots, the culture and tradition through rituals and street dancing. A thanks giving celebration of the Higaonon, meaning “to thank god” for all the blessings, bountiful harvest, successful hunting, expedition, installation of new chieftain, birth of a child and any recoveries from hardships and sickness.

1102400000.name: Kadayawan Festival
1102400000.description: Thanksgiving festival celebrating tribal heritage and harvest.

1108200000.name: P’yagsawitan Festival
1108200000.description: This involves performances by indigenous groups of the area, and harvest-related thanksgiving rituals.

1303900000.name: Feast of the Black Nazarene
1303900000.description: Procession honoring the Black Nazarene in Quiapo.

location.province: NCR, City of Manila, First District (Not a Province)

1303900000.name: Feast of the Black Nazarene
1303900000.description: This feast is celebrated at the heart of Manila- Quiapo. Devotees come from all over the metropolis to participate in this annual event honoring the hundred-year-old statue of the Black Nazarene.

location.province: NCR, City of Manila, First District (Not a Province)

1401100000.name: Panagbenga Festival
1401100000.description: Flower festival with floats and street dancing.

1704000000.name: Moriones Festival
1704000000.description: Holy Week reenactment with Roman centurion masks.

1704000000.name: Moriones
1704000000.description: Witness Marinduque’s captivating Moryonan! Widely known as Moriones, this centuries-old Holy Week tradition comes alive with elaborate Roman centurion costumes and penitential reenactments, culminating in the miraculous healing and conversion of Longinus.

1705200000.name: Sanduguan Festival
1705200000.description: This festival reenacts the first contact between the natives of Mindoro and traders from China.

1900700000.name: Sakayan Festival
1900700000.description: ‘Sakayan’ is the local term for small boat with outrigger used for fishing. With fishing as the primary means of livelihood sakayan’ is symbol of the humble lifestyle of fisherfolks who rely on the generosity of the seas where they draw their sustenance from the sale of their daily marine harvest. The newest festival in the region, it is celebrated with dances accompanied by the rhythmic sounds of drums and kulintangan, a musical instrument of the Muslims.

1900700000.name: Lami-Lamihan Festival
1900700000.description: Began in 1983 by former mayor Wilfrido Furigay, the festival showcases the rich Yakan traditions. This is highlighted by a parade and a horse race.

100000000.name: Pangasinan Bamboo Festival
100000000.dateVenueRaw: August 14 Calasiao and Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan
100000000.description: Pangasinan Bamboo Festival August 12 This is a festival showcasing bamboo products and includes bamboo planting and film exhibitions. Venue: Calasiao and Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan

location.text: August 14 Calasiao and Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan

100000000.name: Pintaflores
100000000.description: This festival is marked by a streetdancing involving the pintados or dancers with tattoos or flowers on their body.

100000000.name: Santa Ipon Festival
100000000.description: This is a thanksgiving celebration highlighted by the catching of the ipon , a small but mysterious fish.

100000000.name: San Fernando Giant Lantern Festival
100000000.dateVenueRaw: Month-long Philippine Christmas Village, San Fernando, Pampanga
100000000.description: This is a lantern showcase where lanterns measuring 14 to 18 feet in diameter delight spectators with their kaleidoscope patterns

location.text: Month-long Philippine Christmas Village, San Fernando, Pampanga

100000000.name: Fiesta de Agoo
100000000.dateVenueRaw: December 5-8 Agoo Civic Center, Agoo Basilica
100000000.description: This features a Lantern festival, the coronation of Miss Agoo, the awarding of Bannuar ti and Dakilang Datu Awards.

location.text: December 5-8 Agoo Civic Center, Agoo Basilica

200000000.name: Sunggod Ta KaManga
200000000.dateVenueRaw: February 18-19 Doña Ressing Park, Quezon Bukidnon
200000000.description: Sunggod Ta Kamanga” is a celebration of Manobo culture. It is a tradition of lumads in preparation of farm activities and farm implements. Live chicken and pig are sacrificed. Their blood spread on farm tools and asking the “Mambabaya’ (GOD) for the safety and for the abundant harvest through rituals. A series of activities highlighted by the street dancing and tableau competition, Paratuan Ritual (installation of New Ethnic Leader), Padtungan ta Kasal Ritual ( A tribal Wedding Ceremony). Tribal people from the Manobo Pulangihon and Manobo Matigsalog of the rich and progressive first-class Municipality of Quezon in the province of Bukidnon were joined by the convergence of over a thousand visitors, spectators, and tourists.

location.text: February 18-19 Doña Ressing Park, Quezon Bukidnon

200000000.name: Halaran
200000000.description: This festival highlights the performance of the history and culture of Capizeños during pre-Hispanic times.

200000000.name: Sinadya
200000000.description: This features a fireworks display, a grand parade, a food festival, and the Capiz dance festival.

300000000.name: Pagoda Festival
300000000.description: In Bocaue, Bulacan, a feast is held in honor of the Holy Cross of Wawa found in the Bocaue River. The main attraction of the affair is the fluvial parade of the pagoda or decorated barge and colorful small boats.

300000000.name: Pangapog Festival
300000000.description: This is a thanksgiving festival for a bountiful harvest highlighting the culture of the Sama, the indigenous people of Samal, as shown in the indigenous sports, and other culture-based competitions.

400000000.name: Pahiyas Festival
400000000.description: Homes decorated with colorful kiping rice wafers.

400000000.name: Mahaguyog Festival
400000000.description: A week – long celebration of the MAHAGUYOG Festival, characterized by street parades, pageantry, and a lot of merry – making. It is an annual festival every Saturday of February as a prelude to the feast day of St. Thomas of Aquinas, the town’s Patron Saint, as a gesture of gratitude and a way of thanksgiving of the farmers for the bountiful harvest of crops they reap the whole-year-round. It also supports the One-Town, One-Product (OTOP) program of the National Government that promotes livelihood and entrepreneurship through agri-tourism.

400000000.name: Centurion Festival
400000000.description: This is believed to be the origin of Marinduque’s Moriones Festival and is as colorful.

400000000.name: Turumba
400000000.description: This is a seven-day feast in honor of our lady of sorrows highlighted by a procession and a dance (to the beat of a turumba song).

400000000.name: Sublian sa Batangas
400000000.description: This coincides with the Foundation Day of Batangas City. It revives the tradition of dancing the subli, which is indigenous to the province.

400000000.name: Sarakiki Festival
400000000.description: The festival features street dancers dressed as cocks swaying to the beat of ancient Samareño instruments.

400000000.name: Feast of San Clemente/ Gigantes
400000000.description: This celebration is marked by giant papier mache effigies, natives in wooden shoes and costumes joining the procession of the statue of San Clemente around town.

500000000.name: Fiesta Tsinoy
500000000.description: A Chinese New Year celebration participated by the Filipino-Chinese community (Albay Chapter) featuring various activities i.e., Dragon/Lion Dance, Chinese Cultural Program, ancestral veneration within a mass, among others.

500000000.name: Cagsawa Festival
500000000.description: The festival commemorates the 1814 catastrophic eruption of Mayon Volcano which buried the Cagsawa church and hundreds of people. To date, the Cagsawa Ruins Park which is one of the popular atractions in Bicol became the center of activities of the week-Iona festivitv.

500000000.name: National Arts Month: Bikol Arts Festival (NAM:BAF)
500000000.description: A month long festival showcasing the region’s arts and culture, crafts and agro-industrial products of the different provinces and cities of the region. It coincides with the celebration of the National Arts Month. Various activities are lined up which include Festival parade, Essay Writing and Poster Making Contest. Laro ng Lahi, Fashion Show, etc.

500000000.name: Ligao Sunflower Festival
500000000.description: A festivity which commemorates the Cityhood anniversary of Ligao. It is highlighted streetdancing showcasing the colorful sunflowers where it abundantly grows along the Kawa-Kawa Natural Park.

500000000.name: Isla Carahan Festival
500000000.description: A celebration of the beauty and bountry of Caramoan Island, highlighting its industrv and cultural heritage.

500000000.name: Alinao Festival
500000000.description: A festival which aims to feature the customs, traditions and cultural arts of Malinaonons, the highlight of which is the Street Dancing Competition.

500000000.name: Mananap Festival
500000000.description: One of the most awaited event in the province of Camarines Norte which promotes local culture and tourism in the municipality of San Vicente,

500000000.name: Rodeo Festival
500000000.description: Hold on to your horses, caballeros, its rodeo time in Masbate once again! Feel the excitement as our local cowboys pit their brains against bovine brawn in western style rodeo events like bull riding and steer wrestling, apart from our local games like the good old carabao race. So put on them boots and saddle up – its gonna be a rope-slingin’, dist- kickin’, cowpunchin’ affair.

500000000.name: Layag Festival
500000000.description: A week-long festivity coinciding with the feast of Our Lady of Penafrancia. The festival name was taken from a local world “layag· or sail boat which is a primitive means of transportation of the early people of Rapu-Rapu. It depicts the peoole’s journey of faith

500000000.name: Pasa Pasa Festival
500000000.description: Held in time for the town fiesta celebration, the festival focus on the advocacy of the LGU in the protection and preservation of its rich natural resources including the manta rays as well as in the promotion of ecotourism attractions in the area.

500000000.name: Butanding Festival
500000000.description: A festival which ushers the •Butanding” (Whaleshark) season and a thanksgiving for its blessings to the people of Donsol. Now that they are back, the festivity features regatta, fluvial parade with boats carrying colorful banners and giant images of the butanding along the Donsol River, a street parade of life-size images of the butandings on floats accompanied by barangay delegations. brass bands, drum and bugle corps, and festival street-dancing continQents.

500000000.name: Isla Rancho Festival
500000000.description: A festival that portrays and reflects the place, people and heritage linking and tie-up semblance of inspiration and pride of the people of San Pascual working as one people towards community development

500000000.name: Palong Festival
500000000.description: Highlighted by a street dancing and agro-industrial fair which expresses local folk’s gratitude for their town’s name etymology and signifies the abundant presence of rooster available in the locality. Held also in celebration of their Black Nazarene’s Feast Day on Mav 13.

500000000.name: Alinsangan “Bowa-bowahan” Festival
500000000.description: A colorful cultural festival of pagan origin, and is derived from the dialect “Alinsangan”, a word that describes the characteristics of the people living the in the early settlements. It is a festival showino fertilitv and thanksgiving.

500000000.name: Pili Festival
500000000.dateVenueRaw: Last week of June Sorsogon City
500000000.description: The festival showcases Pili – an indigenous crop of the Bicol region, particularly abundant in Sorsogon. The festival aims to emphasize its importance, and heightens awareness of the pili’s various economic uses.

location.text: Last week of June Sorsogon City

500000000.name: Naro Festival
500000000.description: Commemorating the Dimasalang town’s founding anniversary, the festival’s highlight is the Street Dancing and showdown competition that will showcase the dance festival of every barangay in the municipality.

500000000.name: Pulang-Angui Festival
500000000.description: The festival was derived from its town’s legend “Pulang-Angui”, a vibrant captivating woman who love to wear red-colored dresses. It celebrates, and depicts the town’s rich and unique socio-cultural talents and qualities of its people, verdant ewco-tourism assests and distinct trade and delicacies of the place.

500000000.name: Tabak Festival
500000000.description: An annual commemoration of the City’s Founding Anniversary and the Feast of Saint John the Baptist, the City’s Patron Saint. It comprises various activities geared towards the preservation of Tabaco City’s rich cultural heritage. The Festival’s highlight is the Tabak Festival Street dancing.

500000000.name: Pinyasan Festival
500000000.description: A colorful festival showcasing the province’ primary agri-product, the sweetest “queen• pineapple called Formosa. Featured are float exhibition, street dancing presentation, agro- industrial fair, talent/skills beauty competition and many more interesting activities.

500000000.name: Ginubat Festival
500000000.description: A festival based on the roots of the town of which its name was derived. It features cultural street parade, exhibit, sail boat race, beauty pageant, fiesta celebration, etc.

500000000.name: Pinangat Festival
500000000.description: The town of Camalig is famous for Bicolanos culinary specialty – the laing or pinangat, hence, the celebration of the festival which also showcases the municipality’s rich cultural heritage. It is also held in conjunction with its town fiesta.

500000000.name: Kamalig Festival
500000000.description: An annual celebration of the foundation day and town fiesta of the Municipality of Camaligan, the highlight of which is the Kamalig Street Dance Competition

500000000.name: Libon Paroy Festival
500000000.description: As the “rice granary of Albay”, the festival reflects on the town’s main source of living, “paroy” or rice. It features various activities including street parade, sports fest, and many more.

500000000.name: Lubid Festival
500000000.description: An occasion of merriment, excitement and reckoning the value of culture, tradition and potentials of Malilipot, The festival’s highlight is the Street Presentation and Exhibition (Sayaw Paralubid). The festival also coincides with the observance of the Feast of Mt. Cam1et that will bring out the spirit of Piety amidst the days of gaiety.

500000000.name: Magalleones Festival
500000000.description: The festival depicts the reputation of the municipality as one of the shipbuilding capitals of the Bicol peninsula during the Spanish colonial period. The celebration honors its Patroness, Our Lady of Mt Cam1el and is highlighted by colorful street dance presentations.

500000000.name: Guinobatan Longganisa Festival
500000000.description: A festival showcasing the cultural and natural heritage of the town, showcasing the unique and tasty longganisa products, with the event’s highlights to include the Street Dancing and the Culinaria Longganisa Cooking and Making Contest. Toe festival also coincides with the town fiesta celebration in honor of its Patroness, the Our Lady of Assumption.

500000000.name: Tig-Aw Festival
500000000.description: An annual celebration of thanksgiving in honor of the town’s Patroness, St. Clare of Assisi. Festival highlights include the Ylau-Raya Grand street Dancing Competition, Special Program in the Arts Dance and Musical Night, Tig-Aw Farmers’ Festival, among others

500000000.name: Coron Festival
500000000.description: A showcase of events highlighted by a street presentation participated in by the town’s different public and private schools and sectors gives a week-long of fun and merriment to visitors and local people. The religious package of devotion and prayer in honor of Albay’s patroness, Nuestra Seiiora de Salvacion (Our Lady of Salvation) is the peak event of the festival, colorfully drawing thousands of devotees and religious groups through a long maritime procession of different local sea vessels on the sea spray of the serene pacific ocean going to the quiet barangay of Joroan, the home of the miraculous image.

500000000.name: Mercedes Kadagatan Festival
500000000.description: It is a fishermen’s celebration of thanksgiving for the blessing and bounty during the seafaring, fishing expedition and fish farming endeavors. The event is also a moment of retrospect and recognition of Mother Nature for having endowed Mercedes with a gift of vast fishery resources, magnificent shorelines and other aquatic potentials and the wise utilization and preservation of ecological balance for the attainment of environmental dignity and beauty.

500000000.name: Mercedes FISHtival
500000000.description: This is a thanksgiving festival by local fisherfolk for blessings received during seafaring, and fish-farming.

500000000.name: Lapay Bantigue Dance Festival
500000000.description: It is a local dance art festival that originated from the graceful movements of hovering birds known as seagulls or the LAPAY, found abundant in Barangay Bantigue, Masbate. Flocks of lapay seagulls created a marvelous scenery and inspired the old folks to come up with a local folk dance, that since then has exited and has become an important aspect of the local culture of the people of Brgy. Banitgue and the entire Masbate.

500000000.name: Traslacion (Penafrancia Festival)
500000000.description: Traslacion is the transfer of the Image of INA from the Basilica to Naga Cathedral, carried by hundreds of male devotees. It marks the start of festivity and the 9-day Novena Mass in honor of the Feast of the Our Lady of Penafrancia, Patroness of the Bicol Region.

500000000.name: Busig-On Festival
500000000.description: A festival based on the epic Busig_on of Labo town, which exemplifies heroism and Bicolano values. The festival features the town’s distinct historical values and sentiments through talent and skills competitions featuring the town’s places of interest.

500000000.name: Hin-ay Festival
500000000.description: This features a cultural show, trade fair, and a street dance depicting the archangels’ victory over the “Black” Angels.

500000000.name: Bicol Food Festival
500000000.description: This is a festival of Bicol cuisine: pinangat and laing, bicol Express, inolokan or tilmak, pecadillo and cocido.

500000000.name: T’boli Tribal Festival
500000000.description: This is a gathering of the major ethnolinguistic groups in the province together with representatives from Davao.

500000000.name: Rahugan Festival
500000000.description: A festival showcasing the culture of Basud. The highlights include the Grand Rahugan ParadeBikol Floksong Singing Competition, among others.

500000000.name: Mambulawan Festival
500000000.description: Held to coincide with the Feast of the Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary, the festival aims to forge unity and cooperation among the local community, promote culture and arts, which are all geared towards advancement and economic growth of the town.

500000000.name: Parau Festival
500000000.description: A 12–day celebration done simultaneously with the Feast of Our Lady of the Pillar. It showcases the town’s cultural heritage and the growing aspirations of its people. During this event. families, relatives and friends get together, renew kinship and enjoy the festivities.

500000000.name: Unod Festival
500000000.description: “Unod” Festival expresses thanksgiving of the people of Castilla, a celebration of the bountiful harvest of root crops of the town and the value of being industrious people.· The festival’s highlight is the street dancing competition.

500000000.name: Guipao Festival
500000000.description: An annual celebration in honor of its Patron, SL Andrew the Apostle. The festival is filled with activities depicting greatness and thanksgiving to the God- given wealth of the sea, the highlight of which is the streetdancing competition

500000000.name: Kamundagan Festival
500000000.description: This features “Kiti-Kiti,” “Pastoras,” Bikol Song Festival, and other cultural events.

600000000.name: Ati-Atihan Festival
600000000.description: Street festival with tribal face paint honoring the Santo Niño.

600000000.name: Ati – Atihan Festival
600000000.description: This is an ancient tradition that celebrates the people of Aklan with indigenous origins, eventually honoring the Infant Jesus, Señor Santo Niño. Today, the Ati-Atihan is observed in modern times as a festival dedicated to the Child Jesus. The term “Ati-Atihan” means “merry-making like the Ati,” referring to becoming like the aboriginal natives who are considered the first inhabitants of Aklan and the entire Western Visayas region. Participants smear themselves with soot to darken their skin and dress in tribal finery, complete with the festival’s iconic tasseled headdresses. The procession begins with the vibrant beat of drums and prominent whistles, later punctuated by energetic shouts of “Hala Bira!” followed by “Viva kay Señor Santo Niño!”

location.text: rd Sunday of January Kalibo, Aklan

600000000.name: Karanowan Fish-Tival
600000000.description: In appreciation of the beautiful God- given nature, the Karonawan Fish-Tival is a celebration of the beauty and bounty of Bato in order to inject and instill the importance of preserving and conserving the these natural resources as major sources of food and as potential tourist attractions.

600000000.name: Ang Pagtaltal
600000000.description: This is a procession of flagellants and devotees in biblical attire that ends in the Balaan Bukid Shrine.

600000000.name: Pangalap Ritual
600000000.description: This is a ritual where believers crawl through the Catilaran cave chanting prayers in the hope of gaining supernatural powers to ward off evil spirits.

700000000.name: Sandugo Festival
700000000.description: Commemorates the blood compact between Sikatuna and Legazpi.

700000000.name: Anibina Bulawanun Festival
700000000.description: This is an eight-day multi-themed annual festival that culminates on the province’s foundation day, March 8. It is a colorful and joyful celebration of the province’s rich agricultural harvests, abundant mineral resources, governance’s feats, trade and tourism fair, and a showcasing of the people’s culture and traditions. The Al-law Ng Kalomonan (Tribal Day) falls on the 7th day of Anibina.

700000000.name: Sinulog de Tanjay Festival
700000000.description: The celebration of the residents of Tanjay, Negros Oriental of this 10-day fiesta features the origin of the old sinulog culture. A parade is held showcasing the clothes locals wear, while the horsefighting presentation re-enacts the battle between the Spaniards and the Muslims.

700000000.name: Aurora Festival
700000000.dateVenueRaw: last Sunday of August to first week of September Tanjay, Negros Oriental
700000000.description: The festival features evening novenas participated in by more than 40 clans, which culminate in a nocturnal fluvial procession at the Tanjay River.

location.text: last Sunday of August to first week of September Tanjay, Negros Oriental

700000000.name: Pasko sa Tanjay Festival
700000000.description: This is a month-long Christmas festivity featuring cultural presentations and contests..

900000000.name: Pasalamat Festival
900000000.description: Celebrated annually every 3rd Sunday of January in honor of Sr. Santo Nino and in commemoration of the arrival of the saint’s image in the Philippines and in the City of Pagadian. The Catholic Church spearheads re­ enacbnent on the arrival of the Sto. Nino image through procession. Pasalamat Festival is highlighted with a fluvial parade (regatta), trade exhibits. the Mutya ng Pagadian beauty pageant, carnival shows as well a a civic military parade.

location.text: rd Week of January Pagadian City

900000000.name: Seafoods Festival
900000000.description: Kagang is a crab specie common to seven (7) coastal barangays of Dapitan comprising Taguillon, Banbanan, Carang & Baylimango. Kagang Festival started way back February 2014 and is celebrated annually since then. The festival features the traditional way of cooking kagang which will be offered for visitor experience. The event was organized to revive the waning interest and preserve authentic and traditional flavorful dishes where kagang is the main ingredient.

900000000.name: Kinabayo Festival
900000000.dateVenueRaw: July 23-27 Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte
900000000.description: Kinabayo is an annual observance of Dapitan City’s Fiesta in honor of Saint James “the Greater and the Moor Slayer”. Held every July, Sinug and Kinabayo have become a festivity. Sinug’ is purely veneration using San Francisco Leaves raised high, dancing through the rhythm of the gong or beating of drums as the throng of devotees brings the saint’s image to his chapel. On the other hand, Kinabayo is a unique dramatization of the triumph of the Catholic faith over Mohammedanism believed to have happened through the intercession of the saint in view of his apparition during the battles of Clavijo and Covadonga and the appearance of the Lady of the Pilar. Modernity has added more color to the festival with the allegorical dance drama presentation of the two events.

location.text: July 23-27 Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte

900000000.name: Dahunog sa Dipolog
900000000.dateVenueRaw: September 26- October 07 Dipolog City, Region IX
900000000.description: “Dahunog” is one of the most ceLebrated festivals in Dipolog where marching bands converge for a parade and compete by showcasing talents to produce the most thunderous, lively and entertaining musical revelry.’ Dahunog [da.ht.i.nug.}is a Cebuano word which means rumbling sound. During the event the city streets resonate with the sounds played by the bands specially the drums, thus the name of the festival.

location.text: September 26- October 07 Dipolog City, Region IX

900000000.name: Kamgbegu Festival (Fest of the Harvest)
900000000.dateVenueRaw: October15-16,2020 Lapuyan, Zamboanga del Sur (Municipal), Region IX
900000000.description: A festival celebrated by people of Duhaylungsod Lapuyan, Zamboanga del Sur who are well known for their peace-loving nature. Through the years, the Subanen’s main source of living is planting rice which is an important aspect of their culture. For the Subanen, harvest season is a time for merrymaking where they come together as one, family and friends, not only for the harvest but also sharing of bountiful blessing, singing, dancing, chanting and feasting altogether on home-made delicacies and ‘pangase’, a rice wine fermented through a traditional process kept and handed down through ancestral lines. The celebration happens every October in time for the harvest season.

location.text: October15-16,2020 Lapuyan, Zamboanga del Sur (Municipal), Region IX

900000000.name: Universal Children’s Festival
900000000.description: The festival involves children of locals, dressed in costumes of UN member countries, parading around the city.

900000000.description: This celebrates the versatility of the Bamboo plant and its importance in the area.

1000000000.name: Festival of Lights Tangub City Charter Day
1000000000.description: A spectacular show of dancing lights is showcased through mass performances of elementary and high school students. Float and arch contests are also held during this time which is participated both by the government and the private sector.

1000000000.dateVenueRaw: February 27 - CANCELLED Maigo , Lanao del Norte
1000000000.description: Celebration of Lanao’s abundance in the Municipality of Maigo through street dancing competition with aqua and agro fair. The search for Ms. Maigo and fashion show using langka is the highlight for promotion of the area.

1000000000.name: Patunob Festival
1000000000.description: A popular religious festival where devotees flock to the shrine of Birhen sa Lourdes to light candles to renew their vows and ask for petitions and blessings. Part of the festival are procession, parade, cultural show, and trade fair. Patunob sa Birhen sa Lourdes is a ritual of healing officiated by women healer devotees of Binuangan. To add, Patunob is a Visayan word for “to be stepped on”. It is a rite where the image of the Blessed Virgin is lightly placed on the person’s shoulders & head.

1000000000.name: Alimango Festival
1000000000.description: An annual celebration that highlights the abundance of Crabs in the Municipality of Lala. Activities include a crab/ocean themed grand street dancing parade, crab races, biggest crab contest and an agri-trade fair

1000000000.name: Hugyaw Sa Kadagatan
1000000000.description: Thanksgiving for the bountiful harvest in line with the Municipality’s foundation day and fiesta which highlight a fluvial parade participated by different barangays in the area.

1000000000.name: Lechonan sa Baroy
1000000000.description: A celebration of bounty of agricultural products with a grand parade of Lechon” – (roasted pig) in the town plaza ornamented with various farm products to showcase the areas rich harvest.

1000000000.name: Grand Kaliga Festival
1000000000.description: This colorful and joyous festival of abundance and prosperity stems from the city’s Manobo and Higaonon roots, the culture and tradition through rituals and street dancing. A thanks giving celebration of the Higaonon, meaning “to thank god” for all the blessings, bountiful harvest, successful hunting, expedition, installation of new chieftain, birth of a child and any recoveries from hardships and sickness.

1000000000.name: Subayan Keg Subanen Festival
1000000000.description: A street dancing and tableau competition which highlights the lifestyles of the Subanons as depicted in songs and dances, and other forms of simulated social expressions, participated by different private schools, 51 Barangays and government contingents using creative costumes and props. It commemorates the anniversary of Ozamiz becoming a chartered city in July 16, 1948. The date also coincides the “FEAST OF OUR LADY OF MT. CARMEL”, the second patroness of the city. It commemorates the anniversary of Ozamiz City becoming a chartered city in July 16, 1948.

1000000000.name: Spring Festival
1000000000.description: A Festival to celebrate the bounty of springs “tuburan” in the area which serves as their major drive for tourism activity and staple income through different mountain resorts. The event is highlighted with a street dancing competition with their own renditions of the story, giving life to how a municipality’s bountiful springs are created participated by different barangays.

1000000000.name: Masskara Festival
1000000000.description: This is a grand Bacoleño celebration marked by carnivals, fairs and masked street dancers.

1000000000.name: Christmas Symbols
1000000000.description: A beautiful Christmas Display in Tangub City, the Christmas Symbols Capital of the Philippines is a holiday tradition inspired by love, value for arts and culture exemplified by the illustrious people of the city through this annual event. How would you like to travel the world while enjoying the holiday season’s lights and colors? At this laid-back city in Northern Mindanao “Tangub City”, you get a passport to be filled with country stamps when you visit famous landmarks adorned with Christmas lights and colors.

1000000000.name: Kahumayan Festival
1000000000.description: A tribute to the hardworking, industrious, rice farmers who contributed to the development and prosperity of the municipality. “Humay” is a Visaya word for rice that is abundant in the area (white rice/black rice).

1100000000.name: P’yagsawitan Festival
